name: general_strategies.json
description: Hypothesis library of 16 strategy archetypes with filters, trade management and regime selectors. Untested candidates, not proven edges.
note: Additional strategies beyond the source documents. All are hypotheses to be tested (see 08). Parameters are starting points, not optimised values.

strategies.name: EMA crossover trend following
rules: Long when EMA20 crosses above EMA50 and price above EMA200; short mirror.
Stop 2*ATR; trail with Chandelier (highest high - 3*ATR).
Exit on opposite cross.
strategies.expected_profile: Win rate 30-45%, winners 2-4R, many whipsaws in ranges.

strategies.name: Pullback to value (EMA/VWAP/structure)
rules: Define trend with higher timeframe EMA slope.
Wait for price to retrace to EMA20-50 zone or prior breakout level.
Enter on trigger candle; stop beyond zone; target previous swing or 2R.

strategies.name: Donchian/Turtle breakout
rules: Enter long above 20-bar high (55-bar for slower), short below 20-bar low.
Exit at 10-bar opposite extreme or 2 ATR trailing stop.
Risk 0.5-1% per trade.
Skip a signal if the previous signal would have been a winner (original Turtle filter) and test whether it helps.

strategies.name: Volatility squeeze breakout
rules: Squeeze when Bollinger Bands inside Keltner Channel or bandwidth in lowest 20% of last 100 bars.
Enter on close beyond bands in direction of momentum (MACD histogram or EMA slope).
Stop at 1.5 ATR or opposite band; trail with EMA20.

strategies.name: Inside bar / NR7 break
rules: Identify an inside bar or narrowest range of last 7 bars.
Buy stop above its high, sell stop below its low; cancel the other when one triggers.
Stop at opposite side; target 1.5-2R.

strategies.name: Bollinger mean reversion
rules: Only when ADX < 20 and EMAs flat.
Long when close below lower band then next candle closes back inside; short mirror.
Target middle band; stop beyond the extreme + 0.5 ATR.
strategies.risk: Fails violently when a trend starts. Hard stop mandatory.

strategies.name: RSI(2) short-term reversion
rules: Trend filter: price above EMA200 for longs.
Long when RSI(2) < 10; exit when RSI(2) > 70 or price closes above EMA5.
Use time stop of 5-10 bars.
strategies.note: Studied mainly on equity indices; test before using elsewhere.

strategies.name: Support/resistance fade
rules: Mark levels touched 3+ times.
Enter on rejection candle at level.
Stop just beyond level; target mid-range.
Stop fading after a close beyond the level.

strategies.name: RSI regime momentum
rules: In uptrend RSI tends to hold 40-80; buy dips when RSI touches 40-50 and turns up.
In downtrend RSI holds 20-60; sell rallies at 50-60 turning down.
Exit on RSI losing regime range or structure break.

strategies.name: RSI/MACD divergence reversal
rules: Regular bearish divergence: price higher high, RSI lower high at a key resistance.
Require a trigger: break of last swing low or bearish engulfing.
Stop above the high; target prior support.
Never trade divergence alone in a strong trend.

strategies.name: Liquidity sweep and structure shift
rules: Mark obvious equal highs/lows or prior day high/low.
Wait for wick to sweep the level and close back inside.
Confirm with break of minor structure in reverse direction (CHoCH).
Enter on retest of the break zone; stop beyond the sweep wick; target opposite liquidity.
strategies.warning: Concepts are subjective; encode objective definitions (swing length, wick ratio) before backtesting.

strategies.name: Session/range-window breakout
rules: Define a fixed window high/low (e.g. first 30 minutes of a session or last N bars).
Trade break with stop at the other side or 1 ATR; target 1.5-2R.
On 24/7 synthetics use a rolling N-bar window.

strategies.name: Grid and averaging (cautionary)
strategies.text: Grids and averaging down show frequent small wins and rare catastrophic losses. If used at all, they need a fixed total risk cap and a hard stop. Prefer not to use.

strategies.name: Martingale (never)
strategies.text: Doubling stake after losses has an enormous drawdown tail and hits account/stake limits. Expected value is not improved; only the loss distribution is distorted.

strategies.name: Scalping (cautionary)
strategies.text: Targets are only a few ticks, so spread dominates. Needs very low cost, fast execution and high win rate. For retail on wide-spread instruments expectancy is usually negative after costs. Test with realistic spreads.

trade_management_library.name: Scale out
trade_management_library.text: Take 50% at 1R, stop to breakeven, trail rest.

trade_management_library.name: Time stop
trade_management_library.text: Exit after N bars with no progress.

trade_management_library.name: Volatility target
trade_management_library.text: Scale size inversely with ATR so each trade risks the same dollar amount.

filters_library.name: ADX filter
filters_library.text: Trend systems need ADX > 20-25; reversion systems need ADX < 20.

filters_library.name: Higher timeframe EMA slope
filters_library.text: Trade only in direction of H1/H4 EMA50 slope.

filters_library.name: ATR percentile
filters_library.text: Avoid trading when ATR is in bottom 10% (no movement) or top 5% (chaos) unless strategy is built for it.

filters_library.name: Spread filter
filters_library.text: Skip if spread is more than 10% of planned stop distance.

filters_library.name: Time-of-day filter
filters_library.text: Only trade windows where journaled stats are positive.

combining_strategies: Use a regime classifier to switch between trend and reversion rules instead of running both always.
Diversify across uncorrelated strategies and markets; correlation between strategy equity curves should be low.
Cap total open risk across all strategies.
